newsitem.title: USA: FCC chief says BT-MCI deal should be cleared.
newsitem.headline: FCC chief says BT-MCI deal should be cleared.

text.p: The nation's top phone regulator said Monday that his agency should approve British Telecommunications Plc's proposed $21 billion merger with MCI Communications Corp. after the carriers promised to take steps to spur global competition.

Federal Communications Commission Chairman Reed Hundt said that based on the commitments, "I personally believe we can and should approve the BT-MCI merger as in the public interest." In a statement, he also called for "swift approval" of the deal.
FCC approval of the corporate marriage -- which was announced last November -- represents the last major regulatory hurdle for British Telecom and No. 2 U.S. long-distance carrier MCI.
Hundt said MCI promised to support efforts by the European Union to give British and other European phone customers equal access to all long-distance carriers.

BT and MCI also promised to make available to competitors sufficient capacity on a key trans-Atlantic submarine cable between the United States and Britain. Underseas cable capacity has been clogged by increasing Internet traffic.

Hundt also cited BT's recent decision to sharply reduce the cost for completing overseas calls to the United Kingdom. The so-called settlement rate has fallen to 7 cents from 11 cents a minute, one of the lowest rates in the world.
And the British government recently agreed to sever all ownership ties with BT, providing added assurance that BT "would not enjoy any special advantages over other U.K. carriers," Hundt said.
